newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo stocks end higher despite blue-chip retreat.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo stocks end higher despite blue-chip retreat.

text.p: Tokyo stocks closed slightly higher on Thursday, helped by a rebound in the financial sector and fresh buying in a wide range of issues. But a retreat in major blue-chip issues capped the upside, brokers said.
The 225-share Nikkei average rose 62.21 points or 0.35 percent to close at 18,093.41, after hovering between 17,970.10 and 18,100.31. Its June futures gained 40 points to 18,080.
"The Nikkei 225 was pinned to 18,000 for most of the session, amid a tussle between profit-taking and buying back," said Masaaki Higashida, deputy general manager at Nomura Securities Co Ltd.

Stocks came under selling pressure when the Nikkei average clawed back above 18,003, where it closed on March 31, the last day of the last financial year, a point where investors held heavy long positions.
Turnover was 435 million shares on Thursday, down slightly from Wednesday's 504 million.
Winners outpaced losers 851 to 262, while 127 issues were unchanged.
On other indices, the broader-based TOPIX index gained 9.61 points or 0.71 percent to 1,366.11. The Nikkei 300 inched up 1.56 points or 0.59 percent to 265.01.
Brokerages topped the list of percentage gainers, followed by transport equipment, sea transport, retailers and construction. Banks were the ninth-largest gainer.
Shares in financial and property-related issues, which participants viewed as having been oversold in recent months, were subject to short-covering.
Nomura Securities Co Ltd jumped 70 yen to 1,260 and Daiwa Securities Co Ltd climbed 46 yen to 775.
Institutional investors were selecting for their portfolios domestic demand-related issues backed by solid earnings, such as chemicals as well as iron and steel.
Mitsubishi Chemical Corp hit a new high for this year of 400 yen, before easing back by the close. Kawasaki Steel Corp also rose to a new high of 366 yen before closing unchanged at 364.

Meanwhile, electronics giant Sony Corp fell sharply, as a pause in the yen's retreat against the dollar and unstable U.S. stocks prompted investors to take profits early. Sony's share price lost 110 yen to end at 8,810.
"While the outlook on currencies is unclear, it is hard to keep buying high-tech shares which ascended on the back of the weakening yen," a broker at a second-tier brokerage said.
"Profit-taking in blue chips (in Tokyo) was prompted by a fall in the Nasdaq," said Nomura's Higashida. The Nasdaq has retreated recently despite the rally by the Dow industrials.
The major declining sectors were precision instruments, rubber, electric equipment and automobiles.
Brokers said that the Nikkei average was likely to stay close to the 18,000 line for the time being, as mixed movements in sectors would continue.
The bottom side is also supported by expectations that fresh money will flow into the market from public funds, they said.
The second section index firmed 16.68 points to end at 1,539.17, with 7.64 million shares traded.
The over-the-counter (OTC) index was up 15.11 points at 1,048.97.
-- Hiroko Nakata, Tokyo Equities Desk +81-3-3432-8027
